summary: Deliberate fork deviations applied at build time. The vendored file itself stays byte-identical to the published one (vendor/manifest.json pins its sha256): (1) the annotation toolbar is CHAT-ONLY — upstream also serves file content, which the sidebar's own 'add to conversation' action already owns, and the right column is refused outright; (2) it is offered for any conversation row; (3) its settle wait is shortened; (4) the toolbar renders extra actions injected by the merged bundle, so one hover box carries both 引用 and 批注.

edits.why: One rewrite of annotationRootOf for the whole chat-only rule. Upstream offers this toolbar for TWO things: conversation rows (assistant-only) and FILE content — documentSourceOf() recognizes the host's text previews ([data-textpreview-plain], [data-document-markdown], [data-code-preview] pre inside [data-textpreview-url]) and its result is preferred over rows. Measured in the field: the merged box appeared over a package-lock.json opened in the sidebar, duplicating dsh-better-sidebar's own 'add selection to conversation' action with 引用 / 侧边对话 — actions that are meaningless for a file. So: (1) document roots are disabled outright — the merged bundle is chat-only (dsh-better-sidebar still owns file content with its own popup); (2) any node inside the right column ([data-slot="sidebar"] / sidebar.*) is refused before the legacy test, because that column hosts file viewers, the side chat and DSH's own right-Sidebar tab types; (3) the conversation-row acceptance now keeps the same right-column refusal in its own walk, so a chat row rendered in the sidebar cannot raise it either. The legacy assistantRowOf() stays first in the fallback chain, so an answer row that carries no data-chat-flow-kind still resolves exactly as upstream.

Upstream waits 250 ms after the selection settles before painting its toolbar, while the quote button appears immediately — a visible stagger. 120 ms keeps the drag/settle guard but makes the two read as one toolbar.

This is the merge: instead of moving two plugins' floating boxes together, the annotation toolbar — one hover box — renders an extra button per action the merged bundle injects. The 引用 button then drives dsh-quote-followup's own insert path. The injected loop is wrapped so a throwing action cannot abort the whole toolbar render.
edits.find:
bar.appendChild(ghostButton(
            already ? null : ICONS.plus,
            already ? t('actions.already') : t('actions.annotate'),
            already ? t('actions.alreadyTitle') : t('actions.annotateTitle'),
            already,
            enterEditing,
          ))
          host.appendChild(bar)

edits.why: The settle only re-validates the selection and paints the toolbar — the state machine still starts on a click — so the toolbar can be painted in the same turn as the selection, which is what makes 批注 and 引用 appear together and immediately (upstream shows it ~120 ms later). Upstream's `rootEl === null` early return is PRESERVED here: this bundle's toolbar is chat-only, and without that return the immediate paint raised the box for every selection on the page. During a drag the existing toolbar is only repositioned, never rebuilt, and while the pointer is still down the paint waits for the release (dragging across a message boundary closed the box and made it flicker).

Because the toolbar is now painted before the settle re-reads the selection, enterEditing must take the live excerpt: otherwise a click right after the drag would annotate the excerpt captured when the toolbar first appeared.

The merged toolbar injects the 引用 action, which runs dsh-quote-followup instead of the annotation flow; the box must close after it the way it does after 批注. This publishes the plugin own closeToolbar for that, because a cleared selection does not close the box by itself.

The settle fires 120 ms after the last selectionchange, which a pause mid-drag can reach: the box would then appear under the held pointer and be closed again on the next drag frame. It now waits for the release.
